title: adaptive_duty_permille accepts negative density (fail-open)
description:
File: python/src/lichen/timing/duty_cycle.py
Line: 45-69

Bug: The function accepts negative density values without validation. Negative density falls into the sparse case (density < 3), returning the maximum budget (20 or 50 permille).

Spec 2a.9 states: "A node MUST use the most conservative (lowest) applicable value when the operating class is unknown."

Current behavior contradicts this - negative density (which indicates an error or unknown state) fails OPEN to maximum budget rather than failing CLOSED to minimum budget (dense case).

Impact: If caller passes erroneous negative density, node allocates maximum airtime budget instead of minimum, potentially causing regulatory compliance issues in dense deployments.

Fix: Add validation to reject negative density or treat unknown/invalid density as dense (fail-closed):
  if density < 0:
      raise ValueError("density must be non-negative")
  # or fail-closed: treat negative as dense
